title: Refactor snippets + quick follow-ups (scratch)
content:
Context:
This is a scratchpad for a small, incremental refactor tied to recent PRs that touched the request routing + cache key logic. High-level goal is to reduce cognitive load in route selection code and make unit tests for cache key variants easier to compose. Keep scope tiny: no interface changes for other teams, prefer internal helpers, and ship follow-ups in separate PRs.

Primary constraints:
- Minimal runtime risk: small diffs, covered by current CI and additional focused unit tests.
- No perf regressions on P95 token latency. We run perf microbenchmarks in a follow-up.
- No canonical API changes. External callers remain the same.

What I observed in the last review:
- Two places compute essentially the same cache key transformation (routes/router.go:line ~312 and cache/keys.go:line ~47). Slight differences (one strips session metadata, other doesn't).
- Tests for the router variants are big fixtures — brittle and duplicative.
- Several TODOs mention "merge with cache key utilities later" but no owner assigned.

Goals for this sprint (small, shipable):
1) Extract a single internal helper BuildCacheKey(ctx, req) that encapsulates common normalization (strip transient headers, normalize model_alias, canonicalize input). Keep it package-private.
2) Replace duplicated logic in two files to call the helper.
3) Add 6–8 focused table-driven unit tests covering: with/without session headers, model_alias present, empty prompt, embeddings path vs generation path.
4) Add a lightweight perf check script (local) to run 1000 generated requests through new code and compare throughput vs master (smoke).
5) Add a follow-up ticket for integrating canonicalization policy with Optimize suggestions (future).

Design notes / rationale:
- Why helper rather than refactor to new public type? Because caller surface is large and we want low blast radius. Helper hides heuristics and keeps migration easy. If helper grows, we can promote to object in next PR.
- Keep normalization deterministic and pure (no global state, no random salts). That ensures stable cache keys and test reproducibility.

Quick checklist for the PR I want to open:
- [ ] Add function BuildCacheKey(ctx context.Context, r *Request) string in internal/cacheutils (new file cacheutils/keys.go)
- [ ] Replace duplicated code in routes/router.go and cache/keys.go to call BuildCacheKey
- [ ] Add unit tests in cacheutils/keys_test.go covering edge cases
- [ ] Add a test table for regression: previous bug where session id leaked into cache key (see ENG-1124)
- [ ] Run `go test ./... -run TestBuildCacheKey -bench=.` locally and capture results in PR description
- [ ] Include short note in PR describing why deterministic normalization matters (link to ENG-1124)
- [ ] Add a note in CHANGELOG under Unreleased -> internal: "Introduce cacheutils.BuildCacheKey to dedupe cache key logic"

Edge cases / unresolved questions:
- Should we normalize punctuation in prompts when computing cache key? Pros: reduces cache misses for minor punctuation variants. Cons: unexpected dedup across semantically different prompts. Default: don't normalize punctuation in this PR. Add as follow-up.
- What about versioning model_alias vs model_id? There is subtle behavior where routed alias maps to different quantization variants. For now, include both alias and canonical model id in the key to ensure safety.
- Rate-limiting hooks: we do not include user-level rate limits in the cache key, but double-check SRE that this doesn't produce cross-tenant collisions. Add SRE as reviewer.

Micro-refactor plan (atomic steps):
A) Create cacheutils/keys.go with helper and godoc. Keep function signature minimal. Example sketch: 
  // BuildCacheKey creates a deterministic cache key for request r.
  func BuildCacheKey(ctx context.Context, r *Request) string {
      // copy relevant fields, normalize model_alias -> canonical_alias, strip transient headers
      // canonicalize prompt whitespace (trim) but do not modify punctuation
      // include model_id, model_alias, truncated prompt hash (sha256 hex of first 1024 bytes)
  }
B) Wire router.go: replace inline key logic with call. Keep old code snippet in comment for 2 PRs then delete.
C) Small tests: table driven. Use t.Parallel() where safe.
D) Perf script: scripts/check-cache-key-smoke.sh (bash) that fires N requests using a minimal harness; prints p95 and mean token latency for simple compare. Not for CI — just local.

Tests to write (ideas):
- TestBuildCacheKey_emptyPrompt -> assert stable key and same for multiple calls.
- TestBuildCacheKey_stripSessionHeader -> create Request with X-Session header and without, expect identical keys after normalization.
- TestBuildCacheKey_modelAliasPriority -> alias + id produce consistent combined key.
- TestBuildCacheKey_promptTruncation -> very long prompt -> key includes truncated prompt hash.
- TestBuildCacheKey_unicode -> handle multi-byte unicode.

PR reviewers to request:
- Joan Park (router ownership)
- Eli Martinez (cache infra)
- sRE oncall (for perf sanity) — @sre-oncall in PR description
- optional: product owner if this could affect billing/observability (unlikely)

Mini risk matrix (quick):
- Logic bug -> could cause cache misses but not correctness regression. Mitigation: smoke perf + unit tests + small rollout.
- Perf regression -> low risk (helper is pure CPU), mitigation: microbench and small canary.
- Cross-tenant collision -> high severity if occurs; mitigation: include tenant id and ask SRE to confirm.

Follow-up tickets (to create after merge):
- FR-206: canonicalize prompt normalization policy (decide punctuation rules)
- FR-207: expose caching instrumentation per-key variant in Console (trace keys sample)
- FR-208: consider moving BuildCacheKey into a shared public package if adopted widely

Notes to self before opening PR:
- Keep diff < 120 LOC ideally.
- Keep helper file small and well-commented.
- In PR description, paste local bench numbers and link to this doc + ENG-1124.
- Put TODO comments for items explicitly deferred (punctuation, public API).

Quick dump of commands I'll run: 
- git checkout -b refactor/cache-dedupe-keys
- edit files, run `make test` and `go vet`
- run `go test ./internal/cacheutils -run TestBuildCacheKey -v`
- scripts/check-cache-key-smoke.sh (capture output)
- create PR, request reviewers, add ENG-1124 link

Loose ideas / future thoughts (brainstorm):
- Could we use a canonicalizer config file (json) that lists normalizers by name (trimWhitespace, trimSession, modelAliasResolution) so behavior is testable and toggleable? If we do this later, we can add a small config struct without changing API surface.
- Consider using a short stable token instead of full sha256 for readability in logs (prefix + shorthex). But ensure collision rates acceptable.
- Down the road we may want a deterministic key for embeddings vs generation; maybe a 1-byte variant prefix in the key to avoid accidental reuse.

Random notes / scratch (keep here until PR is green then delete):
- Remember to update router metrics to include a tag for keying variant (old vs new) so we can compare cache hit-rates in rollout.
- Slack note template: "Heads-up: small internal refactor to dedupe cache key logic (ENG-1124). PR: <link>. Expect no external impact. Please review if you own routing or cache infra."

If I forget anything, ping me in Slack (nikhil) with context "cache-dedupe".

--- end scratch ---
